name: Kund
traditional_function: Dedicated rainwater harvesting reservoir functioning as an artificial perched freshwater lens.
Civic ritual bathing, religious ablution, and sacred gathering associated with temples and community shrines.
Hyper-local potable water reserve specifically isolated from saline or non-potable deep groundwater tables.

engineering_principles.what: Symmetrical stepped terracing sloping inward from four directions at 35° to 45° angles toward a compact central floor.
engineering_principles.why: In arid and semi-arid zones where rainfall is scarce, stored surface water must be concentrated into minimal surface area as depth recedes to limit evaporation.
engineering_principles.how: Each descending terrace steps inward with triangular or square step modules, funneling receding water into a deep central cistern.
engineering_principles.engineering_significance: Minimizes evaporative water loss as reservoir volume depletes while maintaining safe, continuous foot access to the water's edge at all depths.

engineering_principles.what: Rhomboidal and triangular interlocking stone stair configurations arranged along descending revetments.
engineering_principles.why: Continuous straight staircases along steep 45° masonry slopes create lateral slip hazards and concentrated live loads.
engineering_principles.how: Triangular step groupings allow descent or ascent along multiple diagonal vectors, distributing pedestrian live loads and providing three-dimensional stone interlock.
engineering_principles.engineering_significance: Functions as a self-buttressing stepped masonry revetment that resists outward water pressure when full and inward earth pressure when empty.

engineering_principles.what: Paved circular or rectangular catchment apron sloping gently inward toward perimeter inlet apertures.
engineering_principles.why: Unlike baolis that tap regional aquifers, many kunds rely predominantly on pure surface rainwater harvesting.
engineering_principles.how: The surrounding ground apron (paytan) is paved with dressed flagstones treated with impervious lime-ash renders, sloped at 1:50 to 1:100 toward stone intake chambers.
engineering_principles.engineering_significance: Maximizes rainfall runoff collection efficiency (capturing >85% of incident precipitation) while excluding surrounding mud and organic contaminants.

engineering_principles.what: Intake chutes (moris) containing successive stone settlement sumps and perforated stone screens.
engineering_principles.why: Rainwater harvested from open aprons carries dust, leaves, and suspended particles that would decompose and spoil stored water.
engineering_principles.how: Inflow passes through an external silt trap pit where heavy mineral grains settle, followed by passing through carved stone lattice grates that trap leaves and debris.
engineering_principles.engineering_significance: Prevents organic debris from reaching the main holding reservoir, preserving biochemical water quality without synthetic chemicals.

water_management_principles.description: Exclusively captures and preserves rainwater rather than relying on subterranean groundwater inflow.
water_management_principles.hydrological_mechanism: Operates as an impervious perched retention basin; essential in geographic zones where underlying groundwater is brackish, saline, or fluoride-contaminated.

water_management_principles.principle: Controlled Gravity Drainage and Siphon Overflow
water_management_principles.description: Stone overflow conduits (moris) discharge excess water at high-water level to prevent erosion of the surrounding foundation apron.
water_management_principles.hydrological_mechanism: Regulates maximum storage hydraulic head to avoid hydrostatic surcharge behind the upper stepped terraces.

environmental_adaptations: Evolved specifically for semi-arid plains, desert fringes, and pilgrimage centers where large numbers of people gather during religious festivals.
Thermal inertia of the deep stone terraces moderates daily temperature swings, inhibiting microbial bacterial bloom.
Impervious lime plaster lining isolates stored sweet rainwater from contaminated or saline surrounding soil water.

traditional_materials.usage: Stepped revetments, corner bastions, and perimeter paytan.
traditional_materials.traditional_role: High-density stone blocks dressed with precise chamfered edges to withstand high pedestrian friction, hydraulic immersion, and algal growth.

traditional_materials.usage: Reservoir floor and lower submerged step joints.
traditional_materials.traditional_role: Multi-layered fat lime mortar enriched with finely pulverized brick pozzolana (surkhi) and marble dust, hand-compacted and burnished with agate stones for water tightness.

traditional_materials.material_family: Natural Gum and Vegetable Waterproofing Admixtures
traditional_materials.usage: Additive in mortar mixing and surface sealing washes.
traditional_materials.traditional_role: Extracts of methi (fenugreek), guggal (resin), aloe vera, and bel fruit pulp incorporated into lime slurry to reduce capillary porosity and improve water tightness.

construction_features: Symmetrical inverted stepped pyramid basin (square or octagonal footprint).
Intricate interlocking triangular step modules descending on all four facets.
Sloped paved catchment apron (paytan) encircling the perimeter.
Screened inlet chutes (moris) with built-in stone sediment settling traps.
Corner decorative pavilions (chhatris) and access toranas (arched entrance gates).
common_deterioration_factors: Delamination, cracking, and loss of the authentic waterproofing lime render (ghootai) from cyclic drying and wetting.
Dislodgement and rocking of stepped stone blocks due to joint mortar dissolution from submerged hydrostatic pressure.
Eutrophication and severe anaerobic water pollution resulting from religious offerings, decaying flower waste, and organic debris.
Application of non-breathable polymer sealers or Portland cement patches, causing moisture entrapment and spalling of underlying stone treads.
conservation_considerations: Preserve the water tightness of the floor and step terraces; avoid structural punctures that compromise the retention basin.
Re-lay loosened step blocks on breathable, flexible hydraulic lime-surkhi bedding mortar matching original stone compressive strength.
Non-chemical biological water purification: deploy traditional floating wetlands, aeration, and sand-gravel filter beds rather than harmful chemical coagulants.
Re-establish the clean drainage gradient of the surrounding paytan apron to avoid contamination from unpaved peripheral mud.
limitations: Distinction between pure rainwater-holding kunds and spring-fed kunds requires local catchment and hydrogeological tracing.
Waterproofing integrity of floor seals cannot be determined visually and requires non-destructive hydrostatic drop-testing.
Mechanical mortar testing must precede any consolidation to prevent placing overly rigid mortars on ductile historic stones.
